items.title: Alan Raph interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Creed had Verve Records at that time. And every now and then he’d pull some new talent — not new but unknown, relatively unknown. And he pulled in Bob James and Don Sebesky around the same time, gave them both an album... Bob became an international star.

ctx.x: Album was called — gosh I didn’t write down the name of it. © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

Oh it was actually Don’s own band. It was Don’s all-star band, Cycles I think it was. Well Okay. Jimmy Pugh and I were the two trombones and we played mostly baritone horn in that band. Don — it’s an interesting story about Don — back in the 60s I used to do a lot of recording at — what’s his name band — Rudy VanGelder’s. And Creed Taylor used to record from there a lot. Creed had Verve Records at that time. And every now and then he’d pull some new talent — not new but unknown, relatively unknown. And he pulled…
Isn’t that curious because you’ve said that you had gotten to a point where not too much scared you or made you nervous.
